test_behavior_analysis.summary: This reproducer defines a custom `Cow` with an associated-type default, then adds a `ToString` impl for `Cow<str>` and a malformed `Display` impl using an undeclared lifetime and no method body. It targets rustc’s handling of generic defaults, `?Sized`, lifetime resolution in impl headers, and trait checking/completeness, while keeping runtime behavior irrelevant.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern points to an ICE in the coherence/specialization pipeline for `ToString`, triggered while the crate already contains malformed impls that should have been rejected cleanly. The reproducer combines several stressors: a user-defined `Cow` with a default type parameter using an associated type projection (`<B as ToOwned>::Owned`), an impl of `ToString` for `Cow<'_, str>`, and a malformed `Display` impl written as `impl<B: ?Sized> Display for Cow<'a, B> {}` where lifetime `'a` is not introduced. The query stack shows the crash happens in `specialization_graph_of` for `alloc::string::ToString` during coherence, even though earlier stages also report ordinary user errors (undeclared lifetime, missing trait items, etc.). This strongly suggests rustc continues building/inspecting the specialization graph or overlap/coherence data for `ToString` using an impl whose self type or predicates are not fully well-formed due to prior error recovery. The common pattern is an interaction between errorful impl headers, projection-based generic defaults, and the blanket `ToString`/`Display` relationship, causing the next-solver coherence path to operate on invalid or incompletely resolved generic arguments instead of bailing out gracefully.
possible_causes: A defect in coherence/specialization graph construction for `ToString` that does not robustly handle impls with prior header errors (such as an undeclared lifetime in the self type), leading to an ICE instead of emitting only diagnostics.

A bug in the next-solver coherence path when evaluating the `ToString` blanket relation against `Display` for a self type containing a defaulted associated-type projection (`O = <B as ToOwned>::Owned`), especially after error recovery has produced an invalid generic substitution.

Missing validation or early bailout in trait selection/coherence when an impl's self type is ill-formed due to unresolved late/early-bound lifetime parameters, causing specialization graph logic to inspect malformed trait refs.

Improper handling of custom types structurally resembling `std::borrow::Cow` in trait coherence, where projection defaults plus `?Sized` parameters and `str` specialization expose an assumption violation in compiler code that expects fully normalized, well-formed self types.

An error-recovery bug in well-formedness/coherence integration: rustc reports normal E0261/E0392-style errors but still feeds the erroneous `Display` impl into `coherent_trait`/`specialization_graph_of`, where internal invariants about impl completeness or generic parameter ownership are violated.

`B: ?Sized + 'a` and specialization on `str` mean the solver must reason about unsized types, lifetimes, and projections simultaneously, matching the kind of edge case that can break normalization/coherence invariants.

The compiler output says there are ordinary user errors and warnings, yet it still panics; this is characteristic of a compiler bug in error recovery or in later passes assuming earlier-invalid impls were filtered out.

selected_files.reason: The ICE happens in `specialization_graph_of` for `alloc::string::ToString`, so the code that incrementally inserts impls and reasons about overlap/specialization is the most direct suspect. This reproducer likely feeds an erroneous `ToString` impl/self type relationship into specialization graph construction after error recovery, and this file is where such malformed impl interactions can violate assumptions.

The query stack shows `coherent_trait` immediately above `specialization_graph_of`. This module coordinates per-impl coherence checking and is responsible for skipping impls whose trait refs already contain errors; the bug may be that the malformed impl is not filtered out early enough before specialization/coherence processing continues.

The reproducer stresses impl-header well-formedness with an undeclared lifetime `'a`, `?Sized`, and a defaulted associated-type projection. Since `check_well_formed` appears in the query stack, a likely failure mode is that WF checking emits diagnostics but still leaves behind partially invalid impl/type information that later coherence code mishandles.

A central malformed element is `impl<B: ?Sized> Display for Cow<'a, B> {}` where `'a` is never introduced. This file resolves lifetime references into bound variables, so a bug in resolving or recovering from that missing lifetime could produce an invalid trait ref/self type that later crashes coherence/specialization.

The undeclared lifetime error originates in late name resolution. If late resolution/recovery for the free lifetime in the impl header leaves an inconsistent HIR or error placeholder in the impl self type, downstream coherence over `ToString` could ICE instead of cleanly ignoring the impl.

This file performs early impl-specific WF validation intended to reject problematic impls before harder-to-diagnose failures in coherence/trait matching. The reproducer is exactly an impl-header error case, so missing early bailout here could allow malformed impl metadata into specialization graph construction.

The crash only reproduces under `-Z next-solver=coherence`, which points at the newer coherence/trait-solving path. `ToString` coherence depends on evaluating impl candidates and equating trait refs, so next-solver candidate handling for an errorful impl/self type could be part of the failure.

Overlap/coherence checking of trait impls is implemented here, and it is one of the main callers involved when determining whether impls can coexist or specialize. Given the malformed `Display` impl plus the `ToString` blanket relationship, overlap logic may be operating on incompletely well-formed headers.

The custom `Cow` uses a default type parameter `O = <B as ToOwned>::Owned`, so normalization of associated-type projections is part of forming/inspecting the impl self type. If normalization in the trait-selection/coherence path does not handle errorful impl headers robustly, it could contribute to the ICE.

Associated-type projection `<B as ToOwned>::Owned` is a key stressor in the reproducer. Projection handling during trait matching/coherence may be leaving unresolved or malformed aliases in the impl subject, which could then break specialization graph insertion or overlap reasoning.
